headline: Data Center Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the costs of grid infrastructure upgrades for large energy users, such as data centers, away from residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Spanberger's administration, consumer and environmental advocates, some lawmakers, Dominion Energy (for lowering customer costs).
opponents: Data Center Coalition (concerned about bill language).
news_headline: Virginia mulls shifting major grid costs to data centers
news_summary: Virginia regulators are considering how data center developers should bear more of the costs for transmission projects, which have historically been spread across the public, with state residents paying billions since 2021 for data center-related transmission lines. This shift aims to address concerns about cost allocation and affordability due to the data center boom.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water utilities report the monthly water consumption of data centers to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency regarding their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Potomac Conservancy, environmental and water advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (initially questioned being singled out).
news_headline: Virginia to Require Detailed Data Center Water Use Reporting
news_summary: Virginia will begin collecting more detailed data on water usage by data centers and other major customers starting January 1, 2027, under a new law. This legislation, identical to SB 553, aims to provide transparency amid growing concerns about the data center industry's impact on water resources.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles and potential impacts on water, agricultural, and historic resources before approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Localities, residents concerned about noise and environmental impacts.
opponents: Not explicitly stated in provided snippets.
news_headline: Virginia budget mandates data center noise regulations
news_summary: Virginia's new budget includes mandates for the Department of Environmental Quality to regulate data centers' noise levels by 2029, with standards set by 2030, and imposes fines for violations. This addresses rising concerns from residents about noise pollution from these facilities.
